title: the seasons
hook: the first rain brings a craving for fried snacks; Charaka says the body's fire is at its lowest

segments.voice: Yesterday, the seasons in summer: the sun draws the moisture out, so you put it back, and maybe set a cup out for someone else.

The first rain on dry ground has a smell, and it often arrives to cheering. Kids run out into it. Somebody puts a pan of oil on the stove, and within the hour there are pakoras, hot and crisp, and cups of sweet tea, and everyone at the window watching the street turn into a river. A real pleasure. And the old Ayurvedic text has a gentle, slightly inconvenient note about it. Today, the rains.
screen: `THE FIRST RAIN ON DRY GROUND.` → `PAKORAS AT THE WINDOW.` → `A GENTLE, INCONVENIENT NOTE.`

segments.voice: Charaka calls the rainy season varsha. His reading, paraphrased: the body comes into the rains already worn down by the hot months, and then the rain weakens the digestive fire further. The air is damp, the ground gives off vapor, the water is muddied, and the body's qualities are stirred up all at once. So just as the pakoras are frying, the text says your fire is burning low. Its advice: light food, grains kept from an earlier harvest, water boiled or collected clean, a little honey. Go easy on heavy meals, hard exertion and daytime sleep. Keep dry, wear clean, fragrant clothes, and don't wade about in the wet. Notice what the text does and doesn't say. First, the pleasure isn't scolded. The rains aren't bad; the body is tender in them, and asks for care. Second, it's a season for staying in. Travel is hard, the roads wash out, the body is weak. Third, Hindu practice has its own staying-in. Tradition calls a stretch of the rainy months Chaturmas. Some people keep a vow then, giving something up for the season, and wandering renunciants, tradition says, stop wandering and stay in one place until the rains end. Some say Vishnu himself sleeps through these months. A god resting, monks staying put, an old physician advising light food and dry feet: different texts, the same season. Slow down, stay close, wait it out.
screen: `VARSHA: THE RAINS ARRIVE` · `THE FIRE BURNS LOW` · `LIGHT FOOD, CLEAN WATER, DRY FEET` · `CHATURMAS: STAYING PUT`

segments.voice: Decide that for the next while you won't go anywhere, not even in your head to the next thing, and let sounds come and go like rain on a roof. Each time the mind wanders off, bring it home, gently, to the breath. If you pray, say a name of God once, and rest in it.
The seasons. In the rains, Charaka's reading is a weak inner fire and a tender body, answered with light food, clean water and staying close. Today's word.
Your line: the seasons. In the rains, the fire burns low and the body asks for care. Day one thousand three hundred five, done.

howItsDone: People who follow Ayurveda eat lightly in the rainy season, drink boiled water and keep dry, as the classical texts advise; some Hindus keep a vow during Chaturmas, the sacred stretch of the rainy months.

chat.says: Why does Grandma say to eat light when it rains? Pakoras are the best part!
options: Charaka says the rains leave the digestive fire low, so light food and clean water help.
Charaka says rain makes the fire strongest of the year, so heavy food is best then.
Charaka says the rains are a bad season, and any pleasure in them should be given up.
chat.meaning: In Charaka's rains, a body worn by summer meets a fire weakened further, so the text asks for light food, clean water and care, not scolding.

sources.ref: Charaka Samhita, Sutrasthana 6 (varsha: the body weakened by the hot season, the fire further weakened by the rains, all doshas vitiated; light food, old grains, boiled or rain water, honey; avoid day sleep, exertion, river water; keep dry and fragrant)

notes: Charaka Sutrasthana 6 varsha regimen: confirm the paraphrase, including old grains ('grains kept from an earlier harvest'), boiled or rain water, a little honey, avoiding day sleep and exertion, and wearing clean, perfumed clothes.
Trapdoor floor 3: Charaka says strength is lowest at the end of adana and start of visarga (the rains); confirm before keeping 'the body is weakest as the rains begin'.

Chaturmas: name not glossed on purpose (claims rule). Confirm 'tradition calls a stretch of the rainy months Chaturmas', vows during it, wandering renunciants staying in one place, and 'some say Vishnu himself sleeps through these months' (Devshayani to Prabodhini Ekadashi).
